summary: Petition under Section 79(1)(c) & (f) of the Electricity Act, 2003 read with Regulations 41 and 42 of the Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (Connectivity and General Network Access to the Inter-State Transmission System) Regulations, 2022 and Regulation 65 of the Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (Conduct of Business) Regulations, 2023, _inter alia_ , seeking extension of time for submission of land documents under Regulation 11A(1) of the GNA Regulations (as amended) with directions to Central Transmission Utility of India Ltd. to not take any coercive action in the interregnum in relation to connectivity granted to the Petitioners along with consequential relief(s) thereof. The present Petition has been filed by Azure Power India Private Limited (APIPL) and Azure Power Sixty-Three Private Limited (AP63PL) (hereinafter collectively referred to as the “Petitioners”), inter alia, seeking extension/ relaxation of time for submission of land documents under Regulation 11A(1) of the GNA Regulations with directions to Central Transmission Utility of India Ltd. (CTUIL) to not take any coercive action in the interregnum in relation to connectivity granted to the Petitioners along with consequential relief(s) thereof. The Petitioners have made the following prayers: - _(b) Pass an order granting relaxation/extension of the timeline prescribed under Regulation 11A(1) of the Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (Connectivity and General Network Access to the Inter-State Transmission System) Regulations, 2022 for demonstrating availability of 50% of the land required for the Petitioners’ 300 MW Solar Power Project at Raghanesda, Banaskantha, Gujarat, by a period of at least four (4) months from 02.07.2026, i.e., up to 02.11.2026, or such further period as this Hon'ble Commission may deem fit and appropriate in the facts and circumstances of the case;_ - _(d) Pass an order directing the Respondent not to invoke, encash, appropriate or act upon the Land Bank Guarantee bearing No. 820-02-0099525 dated 31.07.2024 amounting to Rs. 30 Crores; and the Connectivity Bank Guarantees aggregating to approximately Rs. 9.5 Crores (with details as set out in paragraph 24) furnished by the Petitioner No. 2 in connection with the connectivity granted under Application No. 2200001107, during the pendency of the present Petition and/or for such extended period as may be granted by this Hon'ble Commission; and_ - _(e) Pass any other or further order(s) as this Hon’ble Commission may deem fit and proper in the facts and circumstances of the present case and interest of justice._ **2.** The Petitioners have also filed 99/IA/2026 seeking urgent listing of the Petition seeking issuance of an interim order restraining the CTUIL from revoking, cancelling, suspending, withdrawing or in any manner adversely affecting the connectivity granted to the Petitioner AP63PL. The Petitioner have made the following prayers: - _(c) Pending disposal of the present Petition, pass an urgent ex-parte ad interim order directing CTUIL not to take any coercive action pursuant to or in furtherance of the alleged noncompliance with Regulation 11A(1) of the GNA Regulations, including invocation and/or encashment of the following Bank Guarantees furnished by the Applicant No. 2 in relation to the aforesaid connectivity:_ - _(f) Pass any other or further order(s) as this Hon’ble Commission may deem fit and proper in the facts and circumstances of the present case and in interest of justice._ - (l) In the absence of intervention by this Commission, the Petitioners would be exposed to the imminent risk of revocation of connectivity and consequential invocation of the Bank Guarantees furnished by it, which would result in grave and irreparable prejudice and would jeopardise the substantial investments already made by the Petitioners. **3.** The Petitioners have reiterated their submissions in the main Petition and mainly submitted as under: _ “The learned senior counsel for the Petitioner submitted that the present Petition has been filed inter alia seeking extension of time for submission of land documents under Regulation 11(A)(1) of the GNA Regulations, with directions to the Respondent/CTUIL not to take any coercive action in the interregnum in relation to the connectivity granted to the Petitioners, along with consequential reliefs. The learned senior counsel further submitted that after the filing of the Petition, the Petitioners have now secured approximately 307 acres of land (as against 268 acres on the date of filing of the Petition) and may be permitted to file their note of submissions updating the status of the land secured by them._ _ 2. After hearing the learned senior counsel for the Petitioners, the Commission directed as under:_ _ (b) The Respondent to file its reply, if any, within two days with a copy to the Petitioners, who may file their rejoinder, if any, within a day thereafter.” _ **7.** Learned counsel for the CTUIL submitted that this is a Petition under Power to Relax and their reply would have been just putting forth the factual information, and it is for the Commission to decide on the relaxation. He also submitted that as the due date is 2.7.2026, generally in such matters CTUIL proceeds for revocation of connectivity as per the provisions of the Regulation, if there is no injunction from any court. **8.** Considering the submissions of Petitioners and Respondent CTUIL, the Commission reserved the matter for Order. **9.** We have considered the submissions of the Petitioners and the Respondent and the # **_Issue 1: Whether the Petitioner may be granted relaxation/ extension of the timeline prescribed under Regulation 11A(1) of the GNA Regulations for demonstrating availability of 50% of the land required for the Petitioner’s 300 MW Solar Power Project?_**
